notes:
Summary:
- Prospect: Nimbus Security Ops (Enterprise healthcare analytics). Large clinical search and triage workflows; HIPAA-awareness required.
- Primary ask: Private VPC deployment with strong audit logging export into their Splunk/Elastic SIEM, AWS KMS integration, and US-only data residency.

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Ravi). High-level architecture brief; preference for customer-managed control plane.
- 2026-02-02: Tech deep-dive (Ravi) — discussed VPC peering, NAT per-subnet, and private endpoints.
- 2026-02-25: Security kickoff (legal + security) — shared Redwood security FAQ (drive link).
- 2026-03-02: Recorded meeting (ff_20260302_98734) — requested SIEM mapping sample and retention SLAs.
- 2026-03-09: Follow-up email with initial KMS integration notes; Nimbus asked for sample log schema including field-level redaction guidance.

Audit logging / SIEM requirements (customer-provided):
- SIEM targets: Splunk (primary), Elastic (secondary). Must support forwarder or S3 export + ingest.
- Export modes: streaming syslog/HTTP event collector OR batched S3 exports (parquet/json) every 5m.
- Retention: immutable audit logs required for 7 years for certain clinical workflows; shorter retention (1y) acceptable for non-PHI metadata.
- Access logs: request-level logs (not full PII), admin console access, service-to-service auth events, key-rotation events.
- Log integrity: signed logs preferred (HMAC) and append-only storage.
- Alerting: early detection hooks for spike in failed auths or model-exfiltration patterns.

Requested log schema (customer-proposed fields - asked Redwood to confirm mapping):
- timestamp (ISO8601), request_id (UUID), customer_request_id (optional), user_id (hashed), model_id, model_variant, prompt_hash (SHA256), token_count_in, token_count_out, latency_ms, output_checksum, response_status, error_code, route (hosted|dedicated|private), infra_region, kms_key_id (partial masked), admin_action (boolean), policy_triggered (list), retention_class (PHI|non-PHI), pii_masking_applied (boolean), raw_payload_ref (S3 path or redact token).
- NOTE: Nimbus explicitly forbids storing free-text PHI in persistent logs. They require prompt_hash + output_checksum approach for reproducible mapping without storing raw prompts.

KMS & key management:
- Primary: AWS KMS (multi-account key policies). Nimbus asked for envelope encryption support + ability to import key metadata into Redwood audit logs (kms_key_id pseudonymized).
- HSM requirement for certain data sets — discuss private HSM integration or BYO-HSM in follow-up.

Security review items outstanding:
- Full SIEM ingest examples (Splunk HEC payload and Elastic ingest pipeline) — ACTION: Redwood to provide mapping + 2 sample events (success + error) by 2026-03-17.
- Legal: SLA/retention language for 7-year immutable logs.
- Ops: Network runbook for VPC peering and egress to their SIEM collectors.
- SE: Verify that per-request logs do not include redacted PHI; confirm how function-calls/tool-calls are logged.

Quotes / customer voice:
- “We cannot keep plaintext clinical notes in logs — need deterministic pointer-level audit instead.” — Head of Security (Nimbus)
- "If you can provide Splunk HEC samples + a KMS test vector, we can move to POC." — Infra lead

POC / evaluation plan:
- POC scope: 2-week private deployment in Nimbus VPC (staging subnet), connect log export to their Splunk dev cluster, run 10k queries/day load to validate latency & log throughput.
- Success criteria: logs arrive within 30s of request, log schema matches sample mapping, no raw PHI persisted, KMS envelope flow validated, retention policy test complete.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver SIEM mapping + Splunk HEC example payloads (SE Ravi) — due 2026-03-17.
- KMS compatibility doc + test vector (security eng) — due 2026-03-20.
- Schedule security review workshop with Nimbus legal & infra — target 2026-03-24.

Internal notes / risks:
- Risk: KMS algorithm mismatch with Nimbus BYO-HSM may require engineering work.
- Risk: Long retention (7y immutable) could increase storage cost; need to propose tiered retention in Redwood Optimize.
- Competitive pressure: Nimbus evaluating Anthropic private deployment and an in-house solution; procurement expected after successful POC.
